browser_tests.coverage: Two profiles per synthetic account; profile-scoped sync_pull_watched_items, sync_pull_watch_progress and sync_pull_library use p_profile_id 1 and 2; add-ons use profile_id 1 and 2 because profile 2 has uses_primary_addons=false. Both round trips B profile 1 -> 2 -> 1 and B -> A were asserted.

browser_tests.title: a synthetic same-profile mutation appears only in an independent receiver context
browser_tests.coverage: The new add-on/watched/progress/Library keys were inserted by the fixture backend, not by an application UI write. A fresh independent B context observed them; a fresh A context did not.

browser_tests.title: expired access with a rejected refresh cannot resume an authenticated session
browser_tests.coverage: Expired synthetic access token plus a revoked refresh response returns to the sign-in screen; profile selection is hidden. This is a local auth-boundary assertion, not measured provider expiry.

browser_tests.title: offline reload cannot complete a new server-valid sync or introduce foreign account data
browser_tests.coverage: Identity requests fail at the network boundary; no new fixture completion is recorded; retained local Library/watched keys remain B-only. Cached local continuity is explicitly not a server-valid session claim.

app_ui: Sign-in, profile selection, profile switching, Library navigation, final-item removal and sign-out are driven through the bundled application UI.
Existing Library deletion/reload and pending-removal cases use the real UI save/remove paths.
fixture_backend: The nonempty add-on, watched-item, progress and Library starting sets are synthetic server responses.
The same-profile new-key propagation case mutates the fixture backend directly; it does not prove an application write path.
Expired/revoked refresh and offline failures are synthetic transport controls.

assertions: Exact synthetic keys are asserted in the DOM and in the relevant localStorage keys (savedLibraryItems, watchedItems, watchProgressItems, installedAddonUrls).
Foreign-account keys are asserted absent after both round trips.
Unknown identity/add-on/catalog routes fail or are recorded as unexpected; no real upstream request is allowed.
Nonempty controls are required; an empty synthetic response cannot satisfy a nonempty assertion.
limitations: Synthetic loopback fixture only. It does not prove deployed Nuvio sync, provider authorization, CORS, real device behavior or real new-device propagation.
No live account, credential, session log, QR or device operation was used.
The fixture does not exercise an application UI write for add-ons/watched/progress; those mutations are explicitly fixture setup.
The offline case asserts absence of a new completed server sync and foreign data, not an offline retry or conflict-resolution guarantee.

acceptance_rows.A3: Synthetic isolation and removal cases pass; the unresolved live post-removal failure remains recorded.
acceptance_rows.A4: Synthetic expired/rejected/offline and lifecycle boundaries pass; measured live refresh remains A8.
